comment: Release conditions for every exact-pinned version in package.json (dependencies, devDependencies and overrides),
plus any override added to clear an npm audit advisory. An exact pin is invisible to update-npm-deps.ps1 - that
script upgrades caret ranges and skips exact versions - so nothing would ever remind you a pin is stale. This file
is what makes that check happen: on every run the script executes each `check` and compares its trimmed stdout to
`expect`. Equal means the pin is still required; different means the condition that justified the pin has changed
and the pin should be re-examined. `check: null` means no mechanical test exists - it is reported for manual review
on every run instead of going quiet. Every exact pin must have an entry here, and every entry must name a package
that is actually present in the declared section; the script reports either mismatch.

@codemirror/state.why: obsidian's peerDependencies names this exact version. A second copy in the tree means two CodeMirror state instances at runtime, so editor extensions would attach to the wrong one.

@codemirror/view.why: Same as @codemirror/state - obsidian peer-pins it exactly, and the view layer must run against Obsidian's own CodeMirror instance.

@puppeteer/browsers.why: Clears GHSA-jmr9-qjv8-65gv (extract-zip unvalidated symlink path traversal, 8 high advisories) and nothing else. extract-zip is vulnerable at every published version, so there is no patched version to override it to, and the direct dependency cannot be bumped either: obsidian-integration-testing is already latest and pins webdriverio, and even the newest webdriverio still reaches extract-zip through @wdio/utils -> @puppeteer/browsers ^2.x. @puppeteer/browsers@3 replaced extract-zip with modern-tar, so forcing 3.x on @wdio/utils - the only consumer left on 2.x - removes the subtree entirely. It also dedupes: puppeteer-core already brings 3.2.0 into this tree, so the override collapses two copies into one rather than adding anything. The major bump is safe because @wdio/utils imports only install, canDownload, resolveBuildId, detectBrowserPlatform, Browser, ChromeReleaseChannel, computeExecutablePath and the InstallOptions type, all still exported by 3.x with compatible signatures, and both packages are ESM-only. NEVER take the `npm audit fix --force` remedy here: it downgrades obsidian-integration-testing from 10.x to 1.1.2. Mirrors the same override in obsidian-dev-utils.
@puppeteer/browsers.manualCheck: The check reads @wdio/utils's own declared range, not a version, because that range is what makes the override necessary. When it moves to ^3 or later, @wdio/utils no longer pulls extract-zip on its own and this override can be deleted along with this entry. A `require('@wdio/utils/package.json')` check would not work - its exports map does not expose package.json - hence the readFileSync form, which resolves relative to the package root the sweep runs from.

deepmerge-ts.why: Clears GHSA-ggr8-5vv4-36mx (deepmerge-ts stack exhaustion when merging recursive object graphs), patched in 8.0.0. Reached only transitively, through webdriverio -> @wdio/config / @wdio/utils / webdriver, and no direct bump gets there: every wdio package still declares deepmerge-ts@^7.0.3, the newest release included. NEVER take the `npm audit fix --force` remedy: it downgrades obsidian-integration-testing from 10.x to 1.1.2. The forced major is safe for these consumers. 8.0.0 breaks by renaming the mergeInfo system and aligning the customization shorthand, and a scan of the whole installed tree found only two bindings in use, `deepmerge` and `deepmergeCustom`. Both `deepmergeCustom` shapes present were run against 7.1.6 and 8.0.1 and produce identical output: @wdio/config's `mergeArrays` handler, which reads `meta.key` and returns `utils.actions.defaultMerge`, and webdriver's `deepmergeCustom({ mergeArrays: false })`. Mirrors the same override in obsidian-dev-utils.
deepmerge-ts.manualCheck: The check reads the range @wdio/utils declares, not a version, because that range is what forces the override. When it moves to ^8 or later the override and this entry can both go. Before lifting it, re-run the deepmergeCustom probe rather than trusting the range alone: @wdio/config passes a handler that reads `meta.key`, and that is precisely the API 8.0.0 renamed, so a regression there would be silent rather than a crash.

obsidian-integration-testing.why: NOT a version pin and NOT an advisory fix: it rewrites obsidian-dev-utils' `peerOptional obsidian-integration-testing` range onto the version this repo actually develops against, which is the only thing that lets npm resolve this tree at all. npm 12 treats a peerOptional that IS present as one that must satisfy, so without this override a plain `npm install` dies on ERESOLVE - `peerOptional obsidian-integration-testing@"^12.3.0" from obsidian-dev-utils@105.0.0` against the root's `^15.0.0` - and every install here needs `--force`, which also silently downgrades any FUTURE peer conflict to a warning. That hidden cost is the reason this is an override rather than a flag in a script. No published obsidian-dev-utils clears it: measured 2026-09-19, 105.0.0 peers ^12.3.0 and 105.1.0 / 105.2.0 (latest) peer ^14.0.0, while obsidian-integration-testing is at 16.0.0. Dropping this repo to obsidian-integration-testing 14 is not the alternative it looks like - two behaviors AGENTS.md records as relied upon arrived in 15.0.0: captureObsidianScreenshot applies the vault-name hide itself (the local copy of that helper is deleted), and labelScreenshot REFUSES an overlong caption where it used to clip one silently, a failure mode that had already shipped a truncated caption once. The override adds and removes nothing: `npm install` reports the tree up to date, 0 packages changed - it relaxes an edge, it does not move a version. `npm ci` was never affected either way, here or anywhere: it replays the lock without re-resolving peers, which is also why this went unnoticed until someone ran `npm update`. The real fix is upstream and is planned: obsidian-dev-utils floating its own obsidian-integration-testing devDependency and letting its peer range move with it, onto one that admits the major this repo installs. When that ships, this override and this entry are deleted together.
obsidian-integration-testing.manualCheck: The check asks the one question that decides this override's fate - does the INSTALLED obsidian-dev-utils' peer range admit the INSTALLED obsidian-integration-testing? - rather than reading either version, so an ordinary obsidian-dev-utils float does not raise a false alarm the way a hardcoded `^12.3.0` expectation would. It prints `false` while the override is load-bearing. When it prints `true`, obsidian-dev-utils has caught up and the override plus this entry must both be deleted - an override is removed as soon as it is no longer needed, not left to accumulate. Re-run `npm install` with no flag afterwards to confirm the tree resolves WITHOUT the override rather than merely alongside it.

smol-toml.why: Clears GHSA-7w5x-hrqm-74c2 (smol-toml denial of service via malformed TOML documents), patched in 1.8.0. Reached only transitively, and no direct bump gets there: markdownlint-cli2 EXACT-pins smol-toml at 1.7.0 - the last vulnerable version - and markdownlint-cli2 0.23.2 is itself already the latest release, so floating it reaches no patch. cspell resolves 1.8.0 on its own, so before this override the tree carried two copies and only the markdownlint-cli2 one was vulnerable; the override collapses them onto the patched version rather than adding anything. The forced minor is safe: smol-toml is a TOML parser markdownlint-cli2 uses only to read its own config file, and 1.8.0 changes no API. NEVER take the `npm audit fix --force` remedy here: it fixes by downgrading.
smol-toml.manualCheck: The check reads the pin markdownlint-cli2 itself declares, not an installed version, because that pin is what makes the override necessary. When it moves off 1.7.0 to anything outside the advisory range `<=1.7.0`, markdownlint-cli2 no longer pulls a vulnerable smol-toml and this override can be deleted along with this entry.

typescript.why: TypeScript 7 (tsgo) breaks this toolchain: @typescript-eslint's parser crashes on the native API, so type-aware ESLint cannot run on 7. @typescript-eslint peer-requires the range below, so 6.x is the last usable major. Hold until obsidian-dev-utils migrates.
